title: China sets up new military academy colleges for AI, drones and discipline
source_used: UA.News (summary of the South China Morning Post report)
key_facts: On Wednesday (30 Sep 2026 by our count) the PLA Army Engineering University set up a College of Unmanned and Intelligent Engineering and two colleges for non-commissioned officers: the Combat Support NCO College and the Technical Support NCO College.
The university was founded in 2017 during President Xi Jinping's military reform and trains engineers, technical specialists and command officers for the PLA Ground Force.
The new unmanned and intelligent engineering college reflects the Chinese military's growing focus on unmanned systems and artificial intelligence.
The same day the PLA National Defence University opened the College of Discipline Inspection, Law and Politics at its Xi'an campus, reorganised from its Political College.
The discipline college is to train military discipline inspectors, improve commanders' legal awareness and teach postgraduate and professional courses, including Yan'an revolutionary history.
UA.News says, citing the SCMP, that it opened amid a large anti-corruption campaign in the PLA in which many senior commanders have been removed.
quote_evidence: China has created new colleges within its military education system to train specialists in artificial intelligence, unmanned systems, technical support and disciplinary inspection, South China Morning Post reports.
The college was opened amid a large-scale anti-corruption campaign in the PLA.
why_it_matters_hint: China's army is adding training for unmanned systems and AI and for discipline inspection during an anti-corruption campaign.
event_date: Wednesday 30 Sep 2026 (calculated from 'on Wednesday' in a 2 Oct 2026 article)
notes: SCMP original returned HTTP 403 (blocked). Wrote from the UA.News relay, which names SCMP as its source; no second outlet found. The SCMP original may hold more detail. The 'Wednesday' date is our calculation.
